problem: How can a new session resume work without cross-tenant access, stale authority or competing workers?
principle: Recheck current session and policy, then claim a task with an expected version and a new run. Conversation text cannot establish execution ownership.
check: Can a new run_id bypass a stale task version?
answer: No. Run identity and task ownership/version checks serve separate purposes.
diagram_title: Session switching, concurrent resume and revocation
scope: Local reference: trusted identity injection and SQLite transactions, without a login server or remote writes.

procedures.failure: Closing a session does not delete tasks.
procedures.case: An expired session fails; a new authorized session can resume.

procedures.failure: Insert failure rolls back; stale workers later require fencing.
procedures.measure: Reject stale versions and rollback failed inserts.
procedures.case: Two v1 claims produce only one v2 transition.

procedures.failure: Do not retain unlimited login tokens.
procedures.measure: No amplification or fresh writes after expiry.
procedures.case: Next-day approval resumes via a worker identity, not yesterday’s browser cookie.
